newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-BOC warns on profits if pound holds.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BOC warns on profits if pound holds.

text.p: British specialist gases company BOC Group Plc said on Tuesday fourth quarter profits would be reduced by around 13 million pounds ($20.6 million) if the pound remained strong.

The firm earlier revealed that the pound's meteoric rise on the foreign exchanges this year had pulled pre-tax profits for the nine months to June 30, 1997 down by one percent to 325.4 million pounds.
BOC said that excluding currency translation effects, pre-tax profits would have been six percent higher in the nine month period.
"If you strip out currency, the underlying performance of BOC has been quite solid," chief executive Danny Rosenkranz told Reuters.
The results were pretty much in line with stockmarket expectations and the company's shares rose nine pence to stand at 1,179 pence initially before standing 2.5 pence down by the afternoon.
Peter Edwards, chemicals analyst at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, said he had expected third quarter profits of 106 million pounds compared to the actual 109 million figure.
Analysts said they expected the shares to run into profit taking if they rose much beyond their initial burst.
The downturn in the translation of overseas earnings back into sterling was mainly affected by the pound's rise against the dollar, South African rand, Australian dollar and the Japanese yen.
Another 13 million pounds was wiped off profits in BOC's health care and vacuum technology businesses during the nine months because of the impact of exchange rate movements on currency transactions.

"If you take the same (sterling) rate as at the end of June then we look for another (translation) impact in the final quarter of between seven and eight million pounds," said BOC finance director Tony Isaac in an interview.
He also added that the company expected a hit of about 5.5 million pounds on the transaction side in the final quarter if the strength of the pound continued.
BOC's Rosenkranz said the company had had a lot of interest in the sale of its healthcare division Ohmeda, which it put up for sale in July.
"Phase one bids are due by the end of August, early September and hopefully at the time we will have a clearer indication of how things look," he said.
Analysts expect the sale to fetch anything between 500 million pounds and one billion pounds.

Rosenkranz said the company did not yet have a clear idea how it would use the proceeds of the Ohmeda sale. "We haven't sold it with the objective of using the money to do some major acquisition......but it makes us more
flexible and we are always looking for ideas."
The healthcare business contributed operating profits of 35.2 million pounds in the nine month period compared with 39.1 million previously.

Elsewhere, profits at the company's gases and related products business rose to 305.4 million from 300.5 million previously, while profits at the vacuum business slipped to 38.6 million from 47.3 million.
BOC said that good results in gases in Europe and the Americas helped offset the adverse impact of translation effects there.
